boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named CU Boulder destinations for studying, making, recreation and campus culture, each supported by a direct university source.

cards.title: Norlin Commons
cards.subtitle: Norlin Library · 1720 Pleasant Street
cards.notes: Bring a project group, reserve a room when eligible, or use the shared work areas and technology support between classes.
cards.short_summary: A library-based hub for collaborative work, study rooms and campus academic support.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder Libraries says Norlin Commons provides collaborative work spaces, technology, reservable group study rooms, IT support and writing help.
cards.access_notes: Study-room reservations are limited to current CU Boulder students; review library access and hours before going.

cards.title: Norlin Library
cards.subtitle: 1720 Pleasant Street
cards.notes: Choose a floor that suits your task, then use the research collections, equipment lending or a librarian consultation for coursework.
cards.short_summary: CU Boulder’s largest library combines study locations with collections and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: The university identifies Norlin as its largest campus library and says it offers five floors of study locations, group rooms and equipment lending.
cards.access_notes: Hours vary and a Buff OneCard may be required for building access; check the library’s current hours before visiting.

cards.title: University Memorial Center
cards.subtitle: 1669 Euclid Avenue
cards.notes: Use the building directory to locate student services, campus programs or an event, then build in time to explore the shared public areas.
cards.short_summary: The UMC is a central campus building for student services, involvement and events.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder describes the UMC as housing student-centered offices and services, plus entertainment, dining and student-organization resources.
cards.source_title: 5 things to know about the UMC | Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: Services, events and building access vary; consult the UMC directory or event listings for the destination you need.

cards.title: The Connection
cards.subtitle: University Memorial Center, Room 105
cards.notes: Plan a low-key group break around bowling, billiards, ping pong, console games or board games; check current hours and rates first.
cards.short_summary: A UMC recreation venue with bowling, games and recurring student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The UMC identifies The Connection as a social recreation center with bowling, billiards, ping pong, video games and board games.
cards.access_notes: Activities have rates and schedules; check The Connection’s current hours and event information before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Alienware Buffalo Esports and Gaming Lounge
cards.title: Alienware Buffalo Esports and Gaming Lounge
cards.subtitle: University Memorial Center, Room 138
cards.notes: Coordinate a shared game session or try the tabletop area, then confirm lounge availability and any use requirements before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A UMC gaming space with desktop stations, laptops, consoles, broadcast space and tabletop games.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder says the lounge includes 17 gaming desktops, three gaming laptops, console games, a broadcast studio and a tabletop game space.
cards.access_notes: The university lists the lounge in UMC Room 138; confirm current operating hours and availability before going.

cards.title: CU Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Visual Arts Complex, east of the UMC
cards.notes: Set aside time to view the current exhibitions, and use the nearby campus transit stop or bike racks when planning your visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus art museum with free admission and changing exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The CU Art Museum states that admission is free for all visitors and identifies its location east of the UMC.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Tuesday–Saturday hours and notes some football-game Saturday closures; verify the current schedule first.

cards.title: Fiske Planetarium
cards.subtitle: 2414 Regent Drive
cards.notes: Pick a public star show, fulldome film or talk, buy tickets in advance when possible, and arrive with time to explore the exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A campus planetarium presenting public science and entertainment programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Fiske lists public talks, fulldome films, star shows and music laser/liquid sky shows, with public programming on scheduled days.
cards.access_notes: Public-show dates and closures vary; tickets are sold online or at the box office, which opens 30 minutes before a show.

cards.title: Student Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: CU Boulder main campus
cards.notes: Choose an activity before you go—climbing, swimming, skating, fitness or drop-in recreation—and check the facility schedule for access details.
cards.short_summary: A recreation complex with climbing, pools, an ice rink, fitness space and indoor activity areas.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder lists a climbing gym, four pools, an ice rink, strength and cardio space, and a turf gym at the Student Recreation Center.
cards.access_notes: Facility use is tied to Rec Center membership or applicable access; verify hours, membership and activity schedules before visiting.

cards.title: Idea Forge
cards.subtitle: Miramontes Baca Education Building · 2445 Kittredge Loop Drive
cards.notes: If you have a design project, ask about applicable workshops, fabrication support or drop-in making opportunities before bringing materials.
cards.short_summary: A cross-disciplinary prototyping facility where students design, build and test ideas.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder describes the Idea Forge as a collaborative prototyping space supporting student teams, courses and design-and-development work.
cards.access_notes: Equipment and fabrication activities may require training, scheduling or course/program access; contact the Idea Forge to confirm options.

cards.title: Center for Community
cards.subtitle: C4C · CU Boulder main campus
cards.notes: Use the building as a planned stop for dining or student-support errands, and check the relevant office or dining listing before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus building that combines dining with student-support offices.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder reports that the Center for Community was designed as a location for students to access dining and multiple student-support services.
cards.source_title: CU-Boulder's New Center for Community Building a One-Stop Shop for Student Services
cards.access_notes: Dining requires payment or an eligible meal plan; individual offices maintain their own hours and access procedures.
